newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Russia oil flows to Europe via Druzhba down in '96.
newsitem.headline: Russia oil flows to Europe via Druzhba down in '96.

text.p: Russian oil flows via Ukraine's stretch of the Druzhba pipeline fell to 16.6 million tonnes (about 332,000 barrels per day) last year compared to 18 million tonnes (360,000 bpd) in 1995, a top pipeline official said on Friday.

Druzhba's (Friendship) deputy director Bohdan Fedushchynsky said the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary and former Yugoslavia were receiving oil, unlike two previous new year periods when supplies fell due to higher transit tariffs.

"Oil is flowing normally and regularly. At this time we are negotiating with Russian suppliers and so far have no fixed contracts for January," Fedushchynsky told Reuters by telephone from the Druzhba headquarters in the western city of Lviv.
Czech customers voiced concern earlier this week about possible reductions of supplies.
About 80 Russian energy firms supply oil via Druzhba.
Fedushchynsky did not exclude the possibility that Druzhba could reduce transit tariffs, raised a year ago to $5.20 per tonne for transit across Ukraine from $4.75 in 1995.
"We will take into account the market situation -- demand, supply and so on. We might consider a lower tariff," Fedushchynsky said.
"We will fight for our clients," he added.
Fedushchynsky's comments contrasted with statements made last month by the pipeline's chief executive about possible tariff increases around the end of February.

Much of Druzhba's total capacity of about 60 million tonnes (1.2 million bpd), which includes the Belarus stretch to Poland and Germany, has not been used since the collapse of the former Soviet Union because many European clients were keen to diversify oil supplies.
